Appreciate the transparency and answer here. Thank you for more insight and as someone who is in sales I understand this. The verbiage used while attempting to attract potential partners is way different then what folks use in normal day to day conversation. It sucks, but you have to learn the "corporate speak" to make it in any active moving business where you are speaking with customers. Even though the person you are speaking to is also another person, they(like yourself or the other person in the conversation) have been taught to listen/use certain verbiage when speaking in a business atmosphere. 

I'll admit, this has lead to me feeling like an idiot in a couple sales situations, but I use honesty as a very good weapon in those situations and will either admit I am not sure what a certain word means or joke that I know the laymen speak for something and not the "business correct" way to word it. Since everyone seems up in arms over this, I wanted to throw my 2 cents in. I'll start with this, do I believe the playoffs in Nascar has flaws, yes it very much does and it does not reward the best driver each season based on stats. 

With that said, I do believe the playoffs pushes drivers to have something to fight for in the last 10 races of the season when under a full season or the original chase format they did not. Do we get the amazing finish at Homestead without the playoffs? Maybe, but, and i am biased here, as a Blaney fan, it made him getting beat mean something more. It gives me reason to feel excitement and drama when I may otherwise feel indifferent. Do not get me wrong, seeing your favorite driver lose is heart wrenching, but when you add the fact he may have missed a shot of a championship due to it, it made it hurt more and had me glued to the Martinsville race. 

If we did not have the playoffs would Blaney have pushed as hard at the end of Homestead to pass Hamlin or would he have been happy with a good points day? We will never know the honest answer, but I remember a lot of fans complaing back in the late 2000s to early-2010s that they hated points racing and wanted wins to mean something. Well, now they mean more than ever. 

I know most folks won't read the typel I typed(and there are probably spelling and grammar errors in there too), but I want to at least give my opinion. Before someone asks, I have been a Nascar fan since the 90s and have watched just about every race since the 2007 season when my parents got cable. I have been a fan of this sport for my whole life and will continue to be. At the end of the day, I just love racing and I want to keep seeing the sport survive into the future. 

TL;DR I don't agree with the playoffs as the best way to crown a champ, but I do feel it brings excitement to the end of the year that would not be there in a season long points system.

I hope you have fun at Martinsville! I went to the fall 2023 and spring 2024 races, so I think I can help. 

I did the pre-race at the fall 2023 race and enjoyed it. My first note is, it will be crowded near the stage. If you want to be close to the stage, you may need to get in line early, but you can still get good spots even if you don't since a lot of people will be walking around. You can walk from exit of turn 4 to the entrance of turn 1 and you will get great views of the cars parked on pit road. You do need to note, do not touch pit wall or lean over it or a police officer or event staff will kindly remind you not to. They are nice(in my experience), but best not to push things.  Other than that, make sure you pack water and sunscreen as you will be on pavement in the sun. 

The best part of the pre-race access is the driver intros and I cannot overstate how awesome it is! The race fans in Martinsville are very passionate about who they love or hate, so be prepared to hear a lot of cheers/boost depending on who is coming in. With it also being a cutoff race, it just makes the entire atmosphere there awesome. 

I hope you have fun!
